s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended which one of the following regarding the Inter-State Council?
o: Transfer of the Inter-State Council to the State List
Immediate establishment of a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263
Replacement of the Inter-State Council by the Finance Commission
Abolition of the Inter-State Council under Article 263
x: The committee recommended the immediate establishment of a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263.
tq: Test the exact constitutional provision and recommended institutional arrangement.
sec: Recommendations - which were and were not made (ISC, 356, AIS, FC, Planning Commission)

s: With reference to Article 356, the Rajamannar Committee recommended:
o: Its complete deletion from the Constitution
Its wider application during constitutional emergencies
Its transfer from the Constitution to ordinary law
Its use only with the approval of the Inter-State Council
x: The committee recommended the complete elimination of Article 356 as part of reducing central control over the States.
tq: Use a direct constitutional-provision question with nearby but reversed recommendations as distractors.
sec: Recommendations - which were and were not made (ISC, 356, AIS, FC, Planning Commission)

s: The Rajamannar Committee viewed the Planning Commission as an extra-constitutional body because it:
o: controlled the recruitment to All-India Services
appointed the Governors of the States
alone decided grants to the States
x: The committee criticised the Planning Commission as an extra-constitutional body that alone decided grants to the States and recommended its abolition.
tq: Identify the specific institutional function attached to the body rather than its general description.
sec: Recommendations - which were and were not made (ISC, 356, AIS, FC, Planning Commission)

s: Which one of the following was recommended by the Rajamannar Committee concerning the Finance Commission?
o: Its transfer to the Concurrent List
Its revitalisation and widening of revenue devolution
Its abolition and replacement by the Planning Commission
Its conversion into a permanent Inter-State Council
x: The committee recommended revitalising the Finance Commission so that States would depend less on the Centre and widening revenue devolution.
tq: Distinguish the Finance Commission recommendation from the recommendation to abolish the Planning Commission.
sec: Recommendations - which were and were not made (ISC, 356, AIS, FC, Planning Commission)

s: The Rajamannar Committee was constituted primarily to study:
o: The recruitment rules of All-India Services
The reorganisation of districts in Tamil Nadu
The distribution of seats in Parliament
x: Its principal task was to study Centre-State relations and recommend measures for greater State autonomy.
tq: Directly test the committee’s terms of reference using related but narrower subjects as distractors.
sec: Terms of reference - why the state set it up

s:
Consider the following statements about the terms of reference of the Rajamannar Committee:
1. It was required to identify the causes of unitary tendencies in the working of the Constitution.
2. It was required to suggest measures securing the utmost autonomy for the States.
3. It was required to strengthen the Centre’s control over education and health.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the committee sought to reduce central control, including over subjects such as education and health.
tq: Separate the autonomy-oriented terms of reference from their exact opposite.
sec: Terms of reference - why the state set it up

s: The Rajamannar Committee sought to secure maximum State autonomy without compromising:
o: The supremacy of the Planning Commission
x: The committee was intended to secure the utmost autonomy for the States while preserving India’s unity.
tq: Test the qualification attached to the demand for State autonomy.
sec: Terms of reference - why the state set it up

s: According to the findings associated with the Rajamannar Committee, the States had effectively become:
o: Territorial units of the Inter-State Council
Subordinate units of the Finance Commission
x: The committee held that, despite the federal form of the Constitution, central dominance had turned the States into administrative units of the Centre.
tq: Use the committee’s distinctive description as a precise recall point.
sec: Terms of reference - why the state set it up

s: Which group of Articles was identified as enabling excessive central intervention in the working of the Constitution?
x: Articles 256, 257 and 365 were identified as provisions that enabled central overreach over the States.
tq: Use an Article-number cluster and distinguish it from other federal provisions.
sec: Terms of reference - why the state set it up

s: The Rajamannar Committee was set up in:
x: The committee was appointed in 1969, although it submitted its report in 1971.
tq: Separate the appointment year from the report year.

s: Who was the Chairman of the Rajamannar Committee?
x: Dr. P.V. Rajamannar, a former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court, chaired the committee.
tq: Use a person–office association question with chairmen of related committees as distractors.

s:
Which of the following persons were members of the Rajamannar Committee besides its Chairman?
1. A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar
2. P. Chandra Reddy
3. R.S. Sarkaria
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and P. Chandra Reddy were the other two members. R.S. Sarkaria chaired a later committee and was not a member of the Rajamannar Committee.
tq: Check committee composition and reject a member borrowed from a related committee.

s: The formal name of the Rajamannar Committee was:
x: Its formal name was the Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee.
tq: Test the official name rather than the popularly used short name.

s: The Rajamannar Committee was set up by the DMK government under:
x: The committee was set up by the DMK government under M. Karunanidhi, who carried forward C.N. Annadurai’s earlier autonomy position.
tq: Distinguish the political leader who constituted the committee from the leader whose earlier view influenced it.

s: C.N. Annadurai’s 1967 view, carried forward by the DMK government, was that the Union need not control subjects such as:
x: The view concerned reducing Union control over subjects such as health and education.
tq: Test the specific examples used to illustrate the autonomy position.

s: Which one of the following is a correct distinction concerning P.V. Rajamannar?
o: He chaired the Rajamannar Committee and also the Fourth Finance Commission.
He was a member of the Fourth Finance Commission but did not chair the Rajamannar Committee.
He chaired the Punchhi Commission and the First Finance Commission.
He chaired the Sarkaria Commission and was a member of the Rajamannar Committee.
x: P.V. Rajamannar chaired the Rajamannar Committee and also chaired the Fourth Finance Commission.
tq: Discriminate between two offices held by the same person and avoid confusing him with later committee chairmen.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the Rajamannar Committee’s position on the Governor?
o: The Governor should replace the elected State government during ordinary disagreements.
The Governor should exercise greater control over State administration.
Central control over the States should be reduced; strengthening the Governor was not sought.
The Governor should be appointed by the Inter-State Council.
x: The committee wanted central control over the States reduced and did not recommend strengthening the Governor system.
tq: Use the ‘not recommended’ distinction in a power-and-authority question.
sec: Recommendations on Governors, Art 356 and AIS

s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended abolition of the All-India Services primarily to:
o: Reduce central administrative control over State governments
Transfer recruitment to the Planning Commission
Create a separate service for each district
Increase the control of the Union over State governments
x: Abolition of the All-India Services was recommended to reduce central administrative control over State governments.
tq: Link the institutional recommendation with its stated federal objective.
sec: Recommendations on Governors, Art 356 and AIS

s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended transferring subjects from the Union and Concurrent Lists to the:
x: It recommended moving subjects from the Union and Concurrent Lists to the State List to enlarge State autonomy.
tq: Test the direction of transfer within the Seventh Schedule.
sec: Recommendations on residuary powers and Seventh Schedule transfers

s:
Consider the following subjects:
1. Stock exchanges
2. Trade unions
3. Electricity
4. Factories
Which of the above were among the subjects proposed for transfer to the State List by the Rajamannar Committee?
x: Stock exchanges, trade unions, electricity and factories were all included among the subjects proposed for transfer to the State List.
tq: Use a list-based question and verify every listed entry before selecting the code.
sec: Recommendations on residuary powers and Seventh Schedule transfers

s: Which one of the following was NOT among the examples of subjects proposed for transfer to the State List?
x: Inland waterway navigation, industrial disputes, and oil fields regulation and development were cited examples. Foreign affairs was not among them.
tq: Identify the unrelated Union subject inserted into a specific transfer list.
sec: Recommendations on residuary powers and Seventh Schedule transfers

s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended that residuary powers should vest in the:
x: The committee recommended that residuary powers should go to the States. This contrasts with the Sarkaria position that residuary powers other than taxation should go to the Concurrent List.
tq: Distinguish the Rajamannar position from the later Sarkaria recommendation.
sec: Recommendations on residuary powers and Seventh Schedule transfers

s: Which one of the following correctly contrasts the Rajamannar and Sarkaria positions on residuary powers?
o: Rajamannar assigned them to the States, whereas Sarkaria placed residuary powers other than taxation in the Concurrent List.
Rajamannar placed them in the Concurrent List, whereas Sarkaria assigned them to the States.
Rajamannar assigned them to local bodies, whereas Sarkaria assigned them to the Union.
Both assigned all residuary powers to the Union.
x: Rajamannar recommended that residuary powers go to the States, while the Sarkaria position concerned the Concurrent List for residuary powers other than taxation.
tq: Compare two similarly named federal-reform positions by isolating the decisive difference.
sec: Recommendations on residuary powers and Seventh Schedule transfers

s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended ending central control over which pair of subjects?
x: The committee sought to end central control over education and health and to move more Concurrent subjects to the State List.
tq: Test the exact subject pair associated with devolution of powers.
sec: Recommendations on residuary powers and Seventh Schedule transfers

s: The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly adopted a State autonomy resolution on the basis of the Rajamannar report in:
x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly adopted the State autonomy resolution in April 1974 on the basis of the report.
tq: Distinguish the resolution year from the committee’s appointment and report years.

s: Which slogan is associated with the DMK’s position on Centre-State relations?
o: Autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre
x: The DMK slogan is ‘autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre.’
tq: Recall the exact wording of a political-federal slogan rather than its general meaning.

s: What was the immediate response of the Union Government to the Rajamannar Committee report?
o: It ignored the report and took no action on it.
It accepted the recommendations on Article 356 but rejected all others.
It referred the report to the Finance Commission for implementation.
It implemented all its recommendations through a constitutional amendment.
x: The Centre ignored the report and took no action on its recommendations.
tq: Test the actual governmental response, not the report’s later influence.

s: The principal historical value of the Rajamannar report lay in the fact that it:
o: Transferred all Concurrent subjects to local bodies
Placed State autonomy on the national agenda
x: Although the Centre took no action, the report placed the issue of State autonomy on the national agenda.
tq: Distinguish direct implementation from agenda-setting influence.

s: The Inter-State Council was established in 1990 through the influence of the:
x: The Inter-State Council was established in 1990 through the influence of the Sarkaria Commission, not directly through the Rajamannar Committee.
tq: Separate an original recommendation from the later body through which it was realised.

s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the report year and Chairman?
1. Rajamannar — 1971 — P.V. Rajamannar
2. Sarkaria — 1988 — R.S. Sarkaria
3. Punchhi — 2010 — M.M. Punchhi
4. Kurian Joseph — Part I, 16 February 2026 — Justice Kurian Joseph
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four pairs are correct: the respective report details are 1971, 1988, 2010, and Part I on 16 February 2026, with the chairmen named in each pair.
tq: Verify both the date and chairman in each committee pair before choosing the complete code.

s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their appointment:
A. Sarkaria Commission
B. Rajamannar Committee
C. Kurian Joseph Committee
D. Punchhi Commission
x: The correct sequence is Rajamannar (1969), Sarkaria (1983), Punchhi (2007), and Kurian Joseph (April 2025).
tq: Fix the earliest and latest committees first, then arrange the two Centre-appointed committees between them.

s: The sequence ‘State, then Centre twice, then a State again’ refers to the appointing authorities of which committees?
o: Rajamannar, Sarkaria, Punchhi and Kurian Joseph
Rajamannar, Punchhi, Sarkaria and Kurian Joseph
Kurian Joseph, Sarkaria, Punchhi and Rajamannar
Sarkaria, Rajamannar, Kurian Joseph and Punchhi
x: The sequence is Tamil Nadu’s Rajamannar Committee, the Centre’s Sarkaria Commission, the Centre’s Punchhi Commission, and Tamil Nadu’s Kurian Joseph Committee.
tq: Use the appointing-authority pattern to reconstruct the chronological chain.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Kurian Joseph Committee in relation to the Rajamannar Committee?
o: It was appointed by Tamil Nadu in 1969 and chaired by P.V. Rajamannar.
It was appointed by Tamil Nadu in April 2025 and consciously followed the Rajamannar approach.
It was established in 1990 to create the Inter-State Council.
It was appointed by the Centre in 2007 and reported in 2010.
x: The Kurian Joseph Committee was appointed by Tamil Nadu in April 2025 and consciously followed the Rajamannar Committee’s approach to Centre-State relations.
tq: Compare a later state-appointed committee with its historical predecessor using appointment year and institutional continuity.

s: The Part I report of the Kurian Joseph Committee was tabled in the Tamil Nadu Assembly on:
x: Part I of the Kurian Joseph Committee report was tabled in the Assembly on 16 February 2026.
tq: Distinguish the report date from the dates of subsequent public references to it.

s: Which one of the following statements about the significance of the Rajamannar Committee is correct?
o: It was the first committee to recommend abolition of the Finance Commission.
It was the first Union-appointed commission on Centre-State relations.
It was the first committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a State.
It was the first committee formed after the establishment of the Inter-State Council.
x: The Rajamannar Committee was the first committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a State.
tq: Use the FIRST distinction to identify the committee’s institutional significance.

s: The Rajamannar Committee provided an intellectual base for later autonomy demands including the:
o: Anandpur Sahib Resolution and West Bengal memorandum
Panchayati Raj Committee and Finance Commission memorandum
Nehru Report and Cabinet Mission Plan
States Reorganisation Commission and Sarkaria Commission only
x: Its autonomy-oriented ideas influenced later demands such as the Anandpur Sahib Resolution and the West Bengal memorandum.
